questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake wear. The four main types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle is too long during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Reduce the length of the load.
Make sure all warning flags and lights are secure and visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all warning flags and lights are secure and visible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is oversize, confirm that all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are secure. Also make sure you have all required permits.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, how should you hold them?

options.text: Between your body and oncoming traffic.
Behind your back so other drivers do not see them until they are placed.
As low as possible to the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between your body and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: To prevent the front tires from skidding.
To prevent the front tires from overheating.
To balance brake use front and back.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves to reduce front wheel skidding. Research has shown these are not needed, so they should be left in the "normal" position.

questions.question: Where is the ABS malfunction lamp on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have a yellow malfunction lamp on the instrument panel. Trailers have a yellow ABS lamp on the left side, either front or rear.

questions.question: What causes the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause trailer rollover is caused by rearward amplification. Different vehicles have different levels of rearward amplification, so know your vehicle's rating.

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing you down, which lane should you use?

options.text: Keep the vehicle in second gear.

questions.explanation: The right lanes are for slower-moving traffic. If a heavy load is slowing you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, which is NOT something you need to check?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: Check that tires have at least 4/32 inch tread on front tires and 2/32 inch on other tires. Make sure tires are not worn, cracked, or over/under-inflated, and that they are all the same size.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Make hand gestures at the driver.

questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Report them to authorities when safe to do so.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the road:

options.text: Should be avoided by leaving the roadway.
Will help your tires grip the road better.

questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. A cardboard box or paper bag might look harmless, but it could hide something hard or heavy that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should:

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to turn.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to turn.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to turn.
questions.explanation: With a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow it. This is different from backing a truck without a trailer.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on hills.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when carrying cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause all air to leak from the brake system, which releases the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: When entering traffic, a large vehicle usually needs:

options.text: About the same space as a car.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space to enter traffic than cars. They are bigger and need a longer distance to speed up.

questions.question: Which part of a combination vehicle is most likely to tip over?

options.text: All parts are equally likely to tip over.

questions.explanation: In double and triple combinations, the trailer farthest from the tractor is most likely to tip over.

questions.question: Stopping distance is affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, weight, and how slippery the road surface is.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from forming in air brakes. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: If your ABS stops working, how should you brake?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down hard.

questions.explanation: ABS is added to your braking system to prevent brake lockup. If it fails, your basic brakes still work, so you can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: How do you warn drivers behind you before braking?

options.text: Tap the brakes a few times.
Stick your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes a few times.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to make your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to finish the trip sooner.

questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, the only safe choice is to safely pull off the road and sleep. Artificial stimulants like coffee can be dangerous because extreme fatigue can occur when they wear off.
